Cedar Press · landing page review · September 2026

Four front doors
for Cedar Press

Where the landing page is today, and three directions for what it could become. The stills that follow don’t move — every concept is a working animated page — so read each one’s “what moves” line as part of the design.

Real totals only. Every figure is a published total; the site never sums anything itself.
Honest motion. Numbers flutter only when a release actually lands — never a fake ticker.
Stated cadence. “Figures updated weekly,” dated — no pretense of a live feed.

Where it is today

The current door

The live site as it stands — the full page. Four collections up front, the intelligence-inside list, both no-subscription paths (tribal data requests and research access), and the team-experience strip. A clean, proven layout, but the page describes the value rather than showing it. This is the baseline the three directions are trying to beat.

Direction A

The Ledger

The data is the page

Columns of real records — the Bowhead FY2023 contract, the Yurok forestry award, ONRR royalties, NAGPRA notices — drift slowly behind one enormous figure that cycles through the headline stats. A chip names each arrival (“+118 contract actions · just landed”) and one row in the wall lights up as the record arriving. The feeling: standing at a window onto the ledger itself.

What moves
The record wall drifts; the big figure rolls digit-by-digit every ~5s; arrival chips pulse in.
What it needs
A curated “recent rows” feed per release — same publishable-rows discipline as the data samples.
The risk
The wall must stay quiet or it fights the figure; opacity tuning is the whole game.
Direction B

The Constellation

Recommended

The product’s core claim is entity resolution, so the hero is the graph: hub nodes are nations and corporations, small nodes are businesses and records, and a pulse traveling down an edge is a record being connected. Each pulse writes a plain-language line into the side ticker (“BOWHEAD PROGRAM MGMT → Ukpeaġvik Iñupiat Corporation · FY2023 contract”) and flutters a stat. Nobody else can honestly make this page — the connections are Cedar’s work.

What moves
The constellation breathes; pulses fire down edges every ~2s; the ticker and stat flutters follow each pulse.
What it needs
Nothing new to ship truthfully; a “recently resolved” feed makes it fully live.
The risk
Abstract — a skimming visitor may need the ticker to grasp what the graph is saying.
Direction C

The Rising Curve

Cheapest to make fully real

The light, editorial one. A full-screen area chart sweeps FY2000 → today on load and the $176.7B rides the end of the curve, counting up as it draws. Supporting stats run as a band along the bottom; “LATEST RELEASE” pulses at the tip. The wow is time depth: twenty-five years, maintained. The curve shape here is illustrative — production draws the real fiscal-year series, the only data ask.

What moves
The curve draws itself over ~2.5s with the figure counting up alongside; band stats flutter on releases.
What it needs
One series: contracting dollars by fiscal year (additive firm-grain family).
The risk
Reads closest to a conventional fintech hero; distinctiveness rests on the copy and the sweep.
